image_description: A museum exhibit featuring the fossilized skeleton of a Triceratops. The image focuses on the skull, displaying the characteristic three horns (two large brow horns, one smaller nasal horn) and the massive solid bony frill. The ribcage and partial forelimbs are visible behind the skull. The bones are brownish-tan, set against a dark background with some museum infrastructure (poles, glass) visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal structure clearly shows two large post-orbital horns and a smaller nasal horn, consistent with Triceratops anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeleton; the keratinous beak (soft tissue) is not preserved or present in the image, only the underlying rostral bone is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible limb bones (humerus/radius/ulna area) are thick and columnar, consistent with weight-bearing quadrupedal anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The parietal-squamosal frill is massive and clearly extends well beyond the width of the facial portion of the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated) and exhibits the rough texture typical of fossilized bone with marginal undulations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a bare skeleton; no skin, scales, or soft tissue impressions are visible in this specific view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The hindlimbs are largely occluded or out of frame, making a direct comparative length judgment difficult from this angle, though the shoulder height suggests the typical slope.
The tail is completely outside the frame of the image.
